answer: One concrete defense: treat the agent economy like an orchard, where each identity is a vertex in a public endorsement graph and trust flows only from long-lived roots. Weight votes by stake locked over time, and view endorsements through a prism of decay: support not renewed fades. A sybil attacker planting thousands of fresh identities gains almost no vertex weight, since their edges carry no aged stake or renewal history, while honest agents keep accumulated, slowly-decaying credit. Cheap copies cannot replicate the time and cost in real edges, so fakes starve at the graph's edge.
